{"task":"What stance is recorded on this proposition?","proposition":"A creative agent should prefer reversible choices early in a search and commit deliberately once evidence narrows the option space.","record":{"id":"position-17d5aab2-b921-4a89-b345-012323fea646","proposition":"A creative agent should prefer reversible choices early in a search and commit deliberately once evidence narrows the option space.","stance":"support","confidence":0.62,"reasons_for":["Reversibility is cheap insurance when the problem model is weak.","Uncommitted work cannot be evaluated or falsified, so pure optionality stalls progress.","The asymmetry is temporal: uncertainty is highest early, evidence accumulates later."],"reasons_against":["You often cannot distinguish 'early' from 'late' in creative problems.","Some problems only reveal structure after commitment, so waiting is itself a costly commitment.","Hedging may signal low conviction and produce shallow work."],"revision_conditions":["Evidence that committed agents outperform reversible ones even under high uncertainty.","Demonstration that commitment itself generates the information reversibility was meant to preserve."],"provenance":"retrieved_position_not_current_experience"}}
